glossary.Subdural space: The potential space between the dura mater and the arachnoid mater.
glossary.Cerebral cortex: The outer layer of grey matter of the brain.
glossary.Venous: From a vein: lower pressure, so blood collects slowly.
glossary.Anticoagulant: A drug that stops blood clotting, such as warfarin, apixaban or dabigatran.
glossary.Anticoagulation reversal: Giving drugs to undo the effect of an anticoagulant quickly.
glossary.Chronic alcohol use: Long-term heavy drinking, which shrinks the brain and stretches bridging veins.
glossary.Multiple falls: Repeated falls, a common clue in older people with a chronic subdural.
glossary.Slurred speech: Unclear speech from weakness or poor coordination of speech muscles.
glossary.Drowsiness: Sleepiness and reduced alertness, an early sign of raised ICP.
glossary.Focal neurological signs: Signs that point to damage in one specific brain area, such as one-sided weakness.
glossary.Hemiparesis: Weakness of one side of the body.
glossary.Unequal pupils: Pupils of different sizes; a late sign of brain compression on one side.
glossary.Subacute: Between acute and chronic; for a subdural, roughly days to a few weeks old.
glossary.Clot evacuation: Surgical removal of a blood clot.
glossary.Coagulation: Here, sealing bleeding vessels with heat during surgery.
glossary.Mass effect: Pressure from a growing lesion pushing brain tissue out of place.
glossary.Neurosurgery: The surgical specialty treating the brain, spine and nerves.
glossary.Clotting factors: Blood proteins that work in a chain to form a clot.
glossary.ICH: Intracranial haemorrhage: any bleeding inside the skull.
glossary.Shearing forces: Forces that slide layers past each other, stretching and tearing vessels between them.
glossary.Haematoma: A collection of clotted blood outside a vessel.
glossary.Haematoma expansion: Growth of a bleed after it starts, worsening pressure on the brain.
glossary.Observation: Watching closely with regular examination instead of treating straight away.
glossary.Recent trauma: A recent injury, such as a fall or blow to the head.
glossary.Rebleeding: Fresh bleeding into an existing collection.
glossary.Neurological outcome: How well brain function recovers after an injury.
